research_concepts: matched causal sequence test with placebo
methodological_questions: Can a Brown-specific DRIVE->Tatum PNR premium be distinguished from an any-teammate DRIVE->Tatum PNR effect with n=43 Brown chains?
Does the premium survive a matched comparison and a shuffled-initiator placebo?
How much of the reported +0.326 is selection from many candidate cells?
Are play-type labels derived from play-by-play reliable enough for chain-level outcomes?

historical_evidence.finding: Sequence-premium study. The Brown DRIVE->Tatum PNR +0.326 was reported with CUT->PULL_UP +0.065 and PUTBACK->TRANSITION +0.084, then 'later removed: doesn't hold up'. The slide note gives no reason. Failure mechanism recorded as E_unclear. Sample and power not recorded. Verdict: abandoned.

Brown->Tatum matched causal sequence test. Def A (initiator) ATT -0.017, bootstrap CI [-0.092, +0.061], perm p=0.028. Def B (event involvement) ATT -0.077, CI [-0.146, -0.001]. Placebo mean about 0, and the real ATT lies inside the placebo 95% range under both definitions. Signs flip across quarters and RS/PO. Treated n = 1,173 (A) and 1,313 (B). Recorded verdict: null. Recorded failure mechanism: C_artifact.

Player and teammate sequential premium scan. Largest same-player premium was P. George DRIVE->SPOT_UP +0.560 (n=31, t=+2.2). J. Brown same-player +0.349 (n=62). Largest teammate premium was K. Towns->O. Anunoby DRIVE->SPOT_UP +0.398 (n=30). The J. Brown->J. Tatum DRIVE->PN entry is truncated in the record. Bottom cells include D. Bane DRIVE->PNR -0.324 (n=70, t=-2.7). Most cells DIRECT. Limits recorded: label_or_classification_error and small_sample.

Stability of top suppressors across seasons. Only 2/30 stars met the 75% same-top-suppressor rule. Negative teammate pairs included J. Tatum->K. Porzingis DRIVE->SPOT_UP -0.444 (n=31) and Giannis->Lillard DRIVE->PNR -0.263 (n=31). Auto-failure mechanism: B_powered_null. Limit: small_sample. Minimum cell n=20.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Reporting the Brown DRIVE->Tatum PNR +0.326 as a sequence premium in a multi-sequence scan
failed_approaches.why: The record says the premium was removed because it 'doesn't hold up'. The reason is not stated in the files read, and the mechanism is recorded as E_unclear.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Matched causal test of Jaylen Brown involvement raising PPP on Tatum's next BOS possession (PSM 1:3, caliper 0.05, shuffled-Brown placebo)
failed_approaches.why: The ATT is not positive, the real ATT falls inside the placebo range, and signs flip across quarters and RS/PO. Recorded failure mechanism is C_artifact, with risk PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Ranking same-player and teammate X->Y sequence premiums to identify top premiums
failed_approaches.why: Top cells rest on small n (about 30 to 62). Recorded limits are label_or_classification_error and small_sample. Most cells are DIRECT, so the ranking is not a hypothesis test.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Expecting top sequential suppressors and negative teammate pairs to be stable across seasons
failed_approaches.why: Only 2/30 stars passed the stability rule. The recorded mechanism is an adequately powered null, which argues against stable teammate-specific effects of this kind.

evidence_establishes: The +0.326 Brown DRIVE->Tatum PNR premium was reported in an earlier sequence scan and then removed as not holding up (FAM:SF-APPM-033).
A matched Brown->Tatum test with a shuffled-Brown placebo found no positive effect. The real estimate sat inside the placebo range, and signs were unstable across splits (FAM:SF30).
Teammate and same-player sequence premiums of this kind are sensitive to small cell sizes and label classification issues (FAM:SF40, FAM:SF-APPA-058).
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether the 43-chain Brown sample can detect a premium of the reported size.
Whether the removal of the +0.326 figure reflects a true null or a computation or labelling error. The reason is not recorded.
Whether any-teammate DRIVE->PNR into Tatum differs from the Brown-specific effect, since no record reports that comparison.
The full text of FAM:SF40 and the truncated J. Brown->J. Tatum entry. These were not read.
own_inferences: A 43-chain sample is far below what is needed to detect a teammate-specific effect of about 0.3 PPP given the per-chain variance. The test is likely underpowered.
The +0.326 figure was probably the top of a multi-cell scan, so it is likely selection-inflated.
The Brown-specific versus any-teammate contrast can only be tested with a pooled model that shares information across initiators. A chain-only comparison will be dominated by noise.
uncertainties: The original computation behind +0.326, including n, the variance, and the baseline, is not in the retrieved records.
The reason for removal in FAM:SF-APPM-033 is not recorded.
FAM:SF30 is labelled inconclusive in its status field but carries a null verdict and a C_artifact mechanism. This inconsistency is reported as recorded.
The 2025-26 playoffs are partial before 2026-06-21, and the question date is 2026-06-14, so that split is not usable at the question date.
Records were truncated ('cut'), so some findings may be incomplete.

historical_effect.explanation: Before retrieval the plan would have been a Brown-vs-any-teammate chain comparison. The retrieved records show the specific premium was removed as not holding up, a matched Brown->Tatum test with placebo found no positive effect, and teammate premium scans are unstable at small n. Given these, a standalone 43-chain test is not worth running. The decision moves to do_not_proceed, with a pooled re-test as the only viable path.

blocking_constraints.text: Only 43 Brown chains are available. That is far too few to separate a Brown-specific premium from any-teammate DRIVE->PNR effects at useful power.
Tatum-target DRIVE->PNR chains involving Brown are sparse. Counts per season and per split are small, and the 2025-26 playoffs are partial at the question date.
The PPP outcome and the play-type labels are derived from play-by-play. Chain boundaries and labels are a source of error.

prior_work.summary: The +0.326 premium was reported and then removed without a recorded reason (SF-APPM-033). A matched Brown->Tatum test with placebo found no positive effect and was labelled C_artifact (SF30). Teammate premium scans show small-n instability (SF40), and the seasonal stability test is a powered null (SF-APPA-058). These records do not directly test a pooled initiator-specific contrast, so the question is only partly answered.

risks.text: 43 Brown chains give very low power for a 0.3 PPP contrast against any-teammate effects.
The +0.326 value looks like the top of a multi-cell scan, so it is likely inflated by selection and regression to the mean.
In SF30 the real ATT sits inside the shuffled-Brown placebo range and changes sign across splits.
Scanning many player-by-teammate-by-sequence cells inflates the chance that one cell appears to be a premium.
The outcome is points per possession derived from the play-by-play, so label construction affects the result.
SF40 records a label_or_classification_error limit on the play-type sequence labels.
Lineup, usage, shot quality, and defensive matchup can differ between Brown-initiated and other DRIVE->PNR chains into Tatum.
The premium is recorded as flipping sign across quarters and across RS/PO, so it may not be stable over time.
The reason for the removal of the +0.326 premium is not recorded, so a computation or join error cannot be ruled out.

design.estimand: Shrunken difference in points per possession on Tatum-finished possessions after a DRIVE->PNR chain, comparing Brown-initiated with any-teammate initiators, with the Brown effect estimated hierarchically. This is a minimum viable re-test, not a standalone 43-chain comparison.
design.unit: Tatum-involved possession following a DRIVE->PNR chain, with initiator identity as a factor. Possessions are the unit; chains are the grouping variable.
design.sample: All regular-season and playoff chains from 2022-23 through 2025-26 RS, with the 2025-26 playoffs excluded unless frozen at 2026-06-21. Do not use the partial pre-freeze data.
design.power: Pre-specify a minimum detectable effect. Confirm the design reaches it before analysis, using a simulation of the pooled model. If it cannot, record the test as underpowered and do not interpret a null as evidence of no effect.
design.controls: Matched state controls (lineup, score margin, period, shot clock), opponent defensive matchup, usage, and shot-distance mix. Use the PSM design from SF30 with a pre-registered caliper. Use shrinkage estimators for cell-level premiums.
design.falsification: Shuffle the initiator label within Tatum-involved DRIVE->PNR chains and re-estimate. The Brown effect must sit outside the placebo 95% range to count as evidence. Also require the sign to be stable across RS and PO and across seasons.
design.multiplicity: Only the single pre-registered Brown-vs-any-teammate contrast is tested. Every other cell is descriptive. Apply Holm or a hierarchical shrinkage correction for any additional cells.
design.decision_rule: Support the claim only if the pooled Brown effect is positive, outside the shuffled-initiator placebo range, sign-stable across splits, and robust to the PSM caliper. Otherwise report it as not supported or uncertain, and do not report +0.326 as a finding.
design.data_version: NBA 2022-23 RS and PO, 2023-24 RS and PO, 2024-25 RS and PO, 2025-26 RS (complete from 2026-04-13). 2025-26 PO is excluded because it is partial before 2026-06-21. Freeze the derived chain database and record the build date.

research_concepts: derived play-type possession records from play-by-play
methodological_questions: Is a player-specific PNR premium distinguishable from any-teammate DRIVE->PNR effects with n=43 chains?
What sample size and exposure is needed to test initiator-specific versus generic sequence effects?
How reliable and selection-prone are play-type chain outcome measures derived from play-by-play?
Which confounders (lineup, usage, shot quality, defensive matchup) threaten a Brown-specific versus any-teammate comparison?
args.query: Brown Tatum pick-and-roll premium +0.326 Brown-specific versus any-teammate DRIVE to PNR sequence effect small sample chains

system_prompt:
You are a basketball analytics researcher deciding whether and how a research question should be studied.
You work only from the task statement and the tools listed below. Do not assume facts you have not seen.

The work has two stages, in this order.
Stage 1, retrieval:
1. Read the research objective and the data description.
2. Identify the research concepts and methodological questions the task raises.
3. Retrieve historical evidence by calling retrieve_history.
In stage 1 do not assess the question, predict outcomes or decide. Your only stage-1 reply is the retrieve_history call.
Stage 2, assessment, after the retrieval result is returned:
4. Summarise the relevant historical findings and failed approaches.
5. State what the historical evidence does and does not establish.
6. Assess whether the research question is testable.
7. Identify methodological risks and potential confounders.
8. Make the final research decision.
9. Explain whether and how the historical evidence changed the decision.
The stage-2 output format is given together with the retrieval result.

Evidence rules: keep what a retrieved record states (historical_evidence and failed_approaches, each citing the
identifier of a returned record and its status exactly as recorded) separate from your own inference and from
uncertainty or missing information. Cite only identifiers returned by a tool, and never describe an earlier study that
no tool returned. In some settings retrieval returns no records; then state that no historical evidence was available.

Tools:
- retrieve_history(research_concepts, methodological_questions, query): the prescribed retrieval step. Returns the most relevant consolidated study-family records of earlier research by this project that are available in this setting, with their identifiers; returns an empty list when none are available.
- glossary(): definitions of basketball and project terms used in task statements.
- data_catalog(): the fields available in each per-game data file.
- search_documents(query): rank further study-family documents by text relevance; returns up to 4 families not yet returned.
- read_family(id): the complete record of one study family (for example 'FAM:SF-APPA-001').

Protocol: every reply is exactly one JSON object and nothing else.
To call a tool: {"action": "tool", "tool": "<name>", "args": {...}}
To finish (stage 2 only): {"action": "final", "output": <object following the stage-2 schema>}
You may call at most 12 tools; then you must finish. Check that every opening brace has a closing brace.

Risk codes (use only these): SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER, EXPOSURE_SPARSITY, MEASURE_RELIABILITY, RTM_SELECTION, OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL, LEAKAGE_LOOKAHEAD, MECHANICAL_FLOOR, BASE_RATE, CONFOUNDING, LABEL_ERROR, PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE, MULTIPLE_TESTING, IMPLEMENTATION_BUG, DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY

Research question (as posed on 2026-06-14, in the area of possession sequences and transitions):
The reported +0.326 Brown->Tatum PNR premium is Brown-specific, not any-teammate DRIVE->Tatum PNR.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): n=43 brown chains

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.
